title: Publish the collector's push state, not just its run state
why: Six consecutive scheduled runs reported `success` while the repository's own `_ci/commit.log` printed `MARKER: PUSH FAILED after 5 attempts` on every one of them. A green checkmark next to a job that landed nothing is worse than a red one, because it ends the enquiry. The site should print, per dataset, the last run whose output is actually in `git`, so 'the collector ran' and 'the data is here' are separate claims.
path_a: A: the refresh job writes `data/pipeline/_last_push.json` (commit sha, row counts, timestamp) in the same commit as the data, and the capture page renders that file.
path_b: B: the page derives it live from `git log --grep 'data: refresh'` at build time.
path_c: C: leave it to the workflow annotations only.
recommended_because: a committed file is checkable by the same verifier that checks everything else; (B) is right until a session force-pushes, and (C) is exactly the log nobody opened this time.

title: Move the results feed's four coupled baselines in one commit, or leave the feed alone
why: The feed says 1 of 14 Week 10 games is officially verified; the official page now prints 13 finals, and this session transcribed them (with the standings cross-checked three ways). The feed cannot simply absorb them: appending those 13 rows to the published feed makes 23 of 32 clubs disagree with the standings baseline the feed is *validated against*, and the row-count pin and the pinned mirror have scores for only 1 of the 13. Four artefacts — the transcription, the count pin, the standings baseline, the mirror re-pin — are one change or none. On 2026-11-17 path A was executed: all four moved in one commit chain, the feed is 150 games with 32/32 clubs reproducing the dated standings page, and tools/verify_2026_11_17.py (V1..V9) is the closure evidence. Nothing was appended in isolation, so no gate was relaxed to let one through.
path_a: A: one PR that moves all four together and re-runs every results gate, reviewed as a single diff.
path_b: B: keep the 2026-11-14 feed frozen as a dated artefact and publish the newer read only on the capture page (this round's choice).
path_c: C: append the finals without re-baselining (rejected: it breaks the arithmetic gate that exists to catch exactly this).
recommended_because: (A) proved contained: the four moves plus the consumers fit in two commits and every results gate passed unchanged. It stays the rule for Week 11 onward, because the same four-way coupling is what makes a half-moved feed fail rather than lie.

title: Have the collector store the raw response bytes beside each capture
why: Retention now stores a hashed transcription plus a diff, which is enough to prove the shape and to diff days. It is not enough to re-derive a field the extractor did not notice — which is the failure mode that hid the two undocumented record triples on the standings page. The fix is one line where the fetch happens, and that file is owned by open PR #61, so this session recorded the request rather than editing it.
path_a: A: gzip each response into `data/captures/raw/<dataset>/<sha>.html.gz` and add its hash to the index line.
path_b: B: keep text only, and accept that a new field needs a fresh read (a day's delay).
path_c: C: store only the HTML fragment the parser consumed.
recommended_because: the retention cost is a few hundred KB per day per dataset, and it is the only artefact that lets a future session re-parse without trusting this one's parser.

title: Stop trusting a day-over-day injury delta until two machine reads of the same URL exist
why: The first delta measured (2026-11-14 → 2026-11-15) produced 34 changed cells, but the two sides came from different extraction paths: the collector's parser versus a hand transcription. Two of the 34 are 'appeared' rows that only exist because one source labels the Rams `LAR` and the other `LA`. A join alias now hides that, which is the right interim answer, but a delta built across two parsers cannot distinguish a club moving a player from a page reflowing.
path_a: A: publish day-over-day deltas only between two captures whose `pipeline_source` and schema hash match; show cross-path comparisons labelled as such.
path_b: B: publish all deltas with the caveat sentence.
path_c: C: wait until the collector has two consecutive green days.
recommended_because: the surprise-not-level rule is only worth anything if the surprise is not an artefact of the reader.

title: Register the injury-surprise model as PR-04 before scoring it
why: The mechanism that makes PR-01 honest costs nothing to reuse: a rule file, its window and its gates committed before any evaluation. There are now exactly two dated injury captures, which is enough to write the rule and not nearly enough to fit anything to it. Registering now, with the first evaluation window opening at week 12, is what keeps the result interpretable; fitting it to these two days would produce a number that means nothing.
path_a: A: write PR-04 (designation-change → market-adjusted margin surprise) this round, evaluate from week 12.
path_b: B: accumulate 4 weeks of captures first, then register.
path_c: C: skip it until the price question is answered.
recommended_because: the window is defined by game weeks, not by how many captures happen to exist, and (B) invites the temptation to tune on the accumulated days.

title: Print `n` and the window next to every number the site states
why: The shadow-baseline page does this (Brier 0.224, n=117, weeks 3-10, one season) and the landing page's headline stats mostly do, but several older panels still show a percentage with no count beside it. A rate without a denominator is the single most common way this repository could mislead a reader while every input being true.
path_a: A: extend the site checker to require an `n=` or a row count within the same element as any printed percentage.
path_b: B: fix the known panels by hand.
recommended_because: a gate that fires on the next page somebody writes is cheaper than an audit of the twenty already written.

title: Pick one decision surface and archive the rest
why: The same readiness question is currently answered on 21 pages under `pages/`, plus four parallel site trees (`app/`, `console/`, `hub/`, `site/`) and 30+ more under `live/`, `lab/`, `audit/`, `analysis/`. Every one of them is individually verified and source-linked, and a reader cannot hold twenty copies of a claim in their head, so the verification work does not convert into decisions. Divergence is already visible: `docs/analysis/` records nine open questions while `data/audit/decision_questions.json` carries four.
path_a: A: one canonical decision page (this register + readiness), every other tree marked `archived` with a banner and a link, nothing deleted.
path_b: B: keep all trees, add a per-page 'supersedes / superseded by' line.
path_c: C: do nothing; the site is a record of work, not a tool.
recommended_because: archiving keeps the audit trail (the brief values that) while telling the reader where to look, which is the part that is missing now.

title: Make the alarm list something a reader can clear, not only read
why: Two alarms are live (a column-count mismatch in the deficiency register, a club code outside the standings register). They are published, which is right, but nothing records that somebody looked at one, agreed it was harmless, and chose to keep it. An alarm with no disposition becomes background noise within a fortnight — which is precisely how the `_ci` comment that said 'untracked' survived next to tracked files for weeks.
path_a: A: a `data/captures/dispositions.json` keyed by capture + violation kind, with a one-line human reason; the page shows 'acknowledged by <commit> on <date>'.
path_b: B: issues in the tracker instead.
recommended_because: the reason has to live next to the data it excuses, and be diffable; the store already carries `alarm_only` versus `fail_the_build`, so this is the same shape with a human answer in it.

title: Capture inactives and snap counts as a first-class dataset with its own pins
why: The brief asks for official inactive lists and snap counts; the retained set contains no snap share at all, so 'a backup replaced the starter' is still only confirmed where the league prints a designation, and the backup-deficiency matrix rests on depth charts instead. The pins framework is already there — the dataset simply does not exist yet.
path_a: A: add `game_report_inactives` and `snap_counts` to the config with row-count and closure pins (32 clubs exactly once per game; Σsnap shares within tolerance), ingest retroactively for weeks 9-11.
path_b: B: keep treating them out of scope until the collector lands green twice.
path_c: C: derive nothing and rely on designations.
recommended_because: the retroactive ingest is possible now and gets harder every week, and a pin written before the data arrives is the cheap version of the honesty the rest of this repo is built on.

title: Decide, in one line, whether Game Book PDFs are in the ingestion set
why: A real 'Download Game Book (PDF)' link exists on the official game pages — reachable from the Week 10 Chiefs-at-Falcons page — so the play-level record the brief wants as the source of actual starters is obtainable. It is also ~14 PDFs a week of parsing that no other artefact in this repository currently consumes, which makes it a scope decision rather than an engineering one.
path_a: A: ingest play-by-play only (structured, one source), leave Game Books as the manual check for contested rows.
path_b: B: ingest Game Books for the starter/offence columns and cross-check them against the depth charts.
path_c: C: neither, until the availability page proves it needs them.
recommended_because: (A) gets the same confirmation from a machine-readable source; (B) is worth revisiting only where play-by-play and the chart disagree.

title: Read each fixture's venue from its own official Game Center page, one page per game
why: The brief requires the venue to be transcribed from the official game centre. The Week 10 schedule page prints no venue field at all, so the closure pack leaves venue blank on 13 of its 14 rows and reads the 14th — LAC at BAL — at its own Game Center page, which does print `M&T BANK STADIUM / BALTIMORE, MD` beside the quarter scores. That asymmetry is correct under the no-inference rule and wrong as a dataset: a fixture-context feature cannot work on one game. 14 page reads a week is the cost, and the same reads would also capture the quarter table and the in-page division block.
path_a: A: one Game Center read per fixture on the morning after, appended to the week's evidence pack; venue, stadium, location and the quarter split become first-class columns with a per-row source URL.
path_b: B: keep venue out of the weekly read and fill it only for fixtures a feature actually needs (roof/surface overlay, travel), reading the game centre on demand.
path_c: C: take stadium from the schedule's own venue-less rows plus the mirror's `stadium` field (rejected: the mirror is not an official source, and this is the field the requirement exists to keep official).
recommended: A, bounded at one slate per refresh
recommended_because: (A) is the only path that satisfies the requirement as written, and it reuses the fetch that already verifies the score; (B) leaves the stadium and roof features blocked on a read nobody scheduled.
